answer_text:
For the parabola \(y^2=4x\), use the standard parametrization
\[
(t^2,\,2t),
\]
and the tangent at parameter \(t\) is
\[
ty=x+t^2.
\]

If the tangent passes through \(P(x_0,y_0)\), then
\[
t y_0=x_0+t^2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
t^2-y_0t+x_0=0.
\]
Let the two roots be \(t_1,t_2\). Then
\[
t_1+t_2=y_0,\qquad t_1t_2=x_0.
\]

The points of tangency are
\[
A=(t_1^2,2t_1),\qquad B=(t_2^2,2t_2).
\]

Now
\[
A-P=(t_1^2-x_0,\,2t_1-y_0)
=(t_1t_1-t_1t_2,\,2t_1-t_1-t_2)
=(t_1-t_2)(t_1,1),
\]
and similarly
\[
B-P=(t_2-t_1)(t_2,1)=(t_1-t_2)(-t_2,-1).
\]

Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
\det(A-P,B-P)
&=(t_1-t_2)^2\det((t_1,1),(-t_2,-1))\\
&=(t_1-t_2)^2(-t_1+t_2)\\
&=-(t_1-t_2)^3.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the area of \(\triangle PAB\) is
\[
S_{\triangle PAB}
=\frac12\left|\det(A-P,B-P)\right|
=\frac12|t_1-t_2|^3.
\]
Since
\[
|t_1-t_2|=\sqrt{(t_1+t_2)^2-4t_1t_2}
=\sqrt{y_0^2-4x_0},
\]
we get
\[
S_{\triangle PAB}
=\frac12\left(y_0^2-4x_0\right)^{3/2}.
\]

For part (2), \(P\) lies on
\[
(x+4)^2+y^2=9.
\]
Since
\[
S_{\triangle PAB}=\frac12\left(y^2-4x\right)^{3/2},
\]
maximizing the area is equivalent to maximizing
\[
D=y^2-4x
\]
on the circle.

From the circle,
\[
y^2=9-(x+4)^2.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
D&=9-(x+4)^2-4x\\
&=9-(x^2+8x+16)-4x\\
&=-x^2-12x-7\\
&=29-(x+6)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(D\) is maximized when
\[
x=-6,
\]
giving
\[
D_{\max}=29.
\]
Then
\[
y^2=9-(-6+4)^2=9-4=5,
\]
so
\[
y=\pm\sqrt5.
\]

Therefore the maximum area is
\[
S_{\max}
=\frac12\cdot 29^{3/2}
=\frac{29\sqrt{29}}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
S_{\triangle PAB}=\frac12\left(y_0^2-4x_0\right)^{3/2},\\[2mm]
P=(-6,\sqrt5)\ \text{or}\ P=(-6,-\sqrt5),\\[1mm]
S_{\max}=\frac{29\sqrt{29}}{2}.
\end{gathered}
}
\]
